newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET - HUDSON, KIRSTEN HIT UNBEATEN CENTURIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - HUDSON, KIRSTEN HIT UNBEATEN CENTURIES.

text.p: Unbeaten centuries by openers Andrew Hudson and Gary Kirsten propelled South Africa to 236 without loss at tea on the first day of the second test against India on Wednesday.
At the interval, Hudson was on 113 and Kirsten had scored 102 after Hansie Cronje had won the toss and elected to bat.
The pair, resuming from 98 at lunch, surpassed South Africa's previous best opening partnership of 155 against India at Port Elizabeth in 1992-93.
Hudson had lucky escapes in the opening session when he twice edged Indian fast bowler Javagal Srinath, who kept a good line and length but got little help from the pitch.
In a surprise move, South Africa omitted Fanie de Villiers from the team. He was replaced by all-rounder Lance Klusener who made his test debut.
De Villiers was the top scorer in the first test in Ahmedabad, which Indian won by 64 runs.
A general strike in Calcutta, which paralysed the eastern city's transport system, did not prevent at least 50,000 spectators from reaching Eden Gardens.
